channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Titans signed OG Peter Skoronski to a four-year, $100 million extension.
item.description: Through three NFL seasons, Skoronski has established himself as a top-tier pass protector and run blocker in the Titans’ left guard spot. His 84.5 PFF pass-blocking grade and 73.2 PFF run-blocking grade from last season are both career highs and compare favorably to his counterparts across the league. His new deal includes $88 million guaranteed.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Seahawks RB Jadarian Price was not seen practicing on Friday.
item.description: No word from the team yet regarding Price’s absence. Hopefully, it’s ultimately a non-issue. Price has occasionally worked with the backups, while diligently refining his receiving skills. However, Price has also been working with the first-team offense, alongside RB George Holani, and was given the first rep in the Seahawks’ first full-team scrimmage at training camp. Holani would benefit if Price is sidelined by an injury. Hopefully, this is not the case.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Broncos WR Marvin Mims left practice early on Friday after suffering an apparent leg injury.
item.description: Mims reportedly pulled up lame while running a deep route. He and TE Nate Adkins, who had also apparently suffered an injury around the same time, took off for the locker room with the training staff. It sounds like a soft tissue injury for Mims. He is currently jockeying for position on the wide receiver depth chart, so hopefully he can return before long.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Raiders WR Malik Benson operated as the team’s WR2 with WR Jalen Nailor and WR Dont’e Thornton “nicked up” on Friday.
item.description: The depth chart placement is a tad curious because it suggests Benson ran ahead of either WR Tre Tucker or WR Jack Bech. Benson has been rotating in with the first-team offense for more than a week, so this isn’t groundbreaking news, but one wonders if he can use the opportunity to make a compelling case for a starting role in three-wide receiver sets.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Saints signed LB Deion Jones, formerly of the Buccaneers.
item.description: Jones played 121 defensive snaps in Tampa Bay last season, totaling 20 solo tackles, one TFL and three quarterback pressures. Jones has now been a member of all four NFC South teams. He will presumably settle into a backup role with the Saints in his age-31 season.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said “we’re taking our time with Tank Dell” as he returns from his knee injury.
item.description: Dell has been on the practice field in a limited capacity for the Texans and is expected to be limited for the next few weeks. The fourth-year receiver missed all of last season due to a horrific knee injury he suffered in 2024 and is hoping to return to action sooner rather than later. On Friday, Dell was non-committal about when he expects to first suit up for a game, but he’s clearly trending in the right direction after an extended time away. Dell returning in any capacity is great news for a player who has had to endure what he went through to make it back, but he faces stiff competition for targets in a wide receiver room that is ripe with playmakers.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Browns waived WR Jamari Thrash.
item.description: Thrash was waived with an injury designation, meaning other teams will have a chance to claim him before he reverts to the Browns’ injured reserve list. In two seasons, Thrash has caught 13 passes for 129 scoreless yards while playing primarily as a backup.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Chiefs HC Andy Reid said the team is “leaning against” playing Patrick Mahomes in next week’s preseason opener.
item.description: Reid said he’s not sure if Mahomes will play at all in the preseason, which doesn’t come as much of a surprise as the star QB continues to work his way back from a torn ACL/LCL he suffered in Week 15 of last season. Despite the late-season injury, Mahomes avoided the PUP list to open camp and has been a full participant thus far. The Chiefs’ first preseason game is scheduled for next Saturday at home against the Rams, with their final game set for August 28th. If we don’t see him over that span, then he will first take the field in Week 1 when the Chiefs play host to the Broncos on Monday Night Football.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: ESPN’s Kevin Seifert says there have been “plenty of indications that Kyler Murray remains the heavy favorite” to win the Vikings’ starting QB job.
item.description: According to Seifert, the Vikings have given Murray “roughly two-thirds of the snaps with the first-team offense in 11-on-11 drills,” while J.J. McCarthy “has spent a significant portion of his summer working with the No. 2 offense.” While reports have been up and down on Murray thus far, Seifert also suggests the gap between Murray and McCarthy remains wide after the first two weeks of camp, saying that “no objective observer to training camp could say that (McCarthy) has made up the ground necessary to truly challenge Murray” this summer. There are still two weeks left to go in camp, but it sounds like McCarthy will need a lot to go right for him to get the nod for Week 1 against the Packers.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Giants WR Malachi Fields “has made an early claim for the No. 2 receiver spot” in camp.
item.description: The Giants traded up to select Fields with the No. 74 overall pick in this year’s draft, adding him to a receiver room that is noticeably thin behind Malik Nabers. This isn’t the first time Fields has garnered praise from the media, as ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported in late July that the Giants were “highly impressed” by the hulking receiver who made a name for himself as a contested catch specialist. It’s highly unlikely that Fields will make enough of an impact as a rookie to be a viable fantasy option, but he could prove valuable as a big target in and around the end zone for the Giants this season.-Zachary Krueger
